simple.meaning: יָנַח (yânach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to deposit ; by implication, to allow to stay.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 75 times in Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and 17 more, beginning at Genesis 2:15. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָנַח (H3240) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָנַח (yânach) / H3240 is traced through Genesis 2:15, Genesis 19:16, Genesis 39:16, Genesis 42:33 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to deposit ; by implication, to allow to stay
definitions.usage: bestow, cast down, lay (down, up), leave (off), let alone (remain), pacify, place, put, set (down), suffer, withdraw, withhold. (The Hiphil forms with the dagesh are here referred to, in accordance with the older grammarians; but if any distinction of the kind is to be made, these should rather be referred to 5117 , and the others here.)
definitions.full: to deposit ; by implication, to allow to stay
